claim: AWS strongly recommends IKEv2 for a Site-to-Site VPN connection and says to use IKEv1 only if the customer gateway device does not support IKEv2.
question: Which IKE version does AWS recommend for Site-to-Site VPN?

values.display: We strongly recommend using IKEv2
only use IKEv1 if your customer gateway device does not support IKEv2

evidence.quote: We strongly recommend using IKEv2 for your Site-to-Site VPN connection. IKEv2 is a simpler, more robust, and more secure protocol than IKEv1. You should only use IKEv1 if your customer gateway device does not support IKEv2.

claim: If you place the customer gateway behind a router or firewall that does NAT, you give AWS the public IP address of the NAT device.

claim: If you do not plan to use NAT-T, you must disable it on your device. Otherwise AWS tries to establish the tunnel over UDP port 4500, and the tunnel does not establish if that port is not open.

values.display: we will attempt to establish a tunnel over UDP port 4500
If that port is not open the tunnel will not establish

evidence.quote: You will need to disable NAT-T on your device. If you don’t plan on using NAT-T and it is not disabled on your device, we will attempt to establish a tunnel over UDP port 4500. If that port is not open the tunnel will not establish.

claim: If the customer gateway device is behind a firewall or other device that uses NAT, it must have an identity (IDr) configured.

claim: The AWS VPN service is route-based. If a device uses a policy-based solution, you need to limit it to a single security association.
question: Does Site-to-Site VPN support policy-based VPN devices?

values.display: the service is a route-based solution
you will need to limit to a single SA

evidence.quote: The AWS VPN service is a route-based solution, so when using a route-based configuration you will not run into SA limitations. If, however, you are using a policy-based solution you will need to limit to a single SA, as the service is a route-based solution.

claim: A device that supports dynamically routed Site-to-Site VPN connections must be able to establish BGP peering, bind tunnels to logical interfaces (route-based VPN), and use IPsec Dead Peer Detection.
question: What must a customer gateway device support for a dynamically routed VPN connection?

values.display: Establish Border Gateway Protocol (BGP) peering
Utilize IPsec Dead Peer Detection

qualifiers.scope: customer gateway devices for dynamically routed connections

evidence.quote:
In addition to the above capabilities, devices supporting dynamically-routed Site-to-Site VPN connections must be able to:
Establish Border Gateway Protocol (BGP) peering
Bind tunnels to logical interfaces (route-based VPN)
Utilize IPsec Dead Peer Detection

claim: If the customer gateway device supports BGP, specify dynamic routing. If the device does not support BGP, specify static routing.
question: When do you choose dynamic routing and when static routing for a Site-to-Site VPN connection?

values.display: If your customer gateway device supports Border Gateway Protocol (BGP), specify dynamic routing
If your customer gateway device does not support BGP, specify static routing

evidence.quote: If your customer gateway device supports Border Gateway Protocol (BGP), specify dynamic routing when you configure your Site-to-Site VPN connection. If your customer gateway device does not support BGP, specify static routing.

claim: AWS recommends BGP-capable devices when available, because BGP offers robust liveness detection checks that can help failover to the second VPN tunnel when the first goes down.
question: Why does AWS recommend BGP-capable customer gateway devices for Site-to-Site VPN?

values.display: We recommend that you use BGP-capable devices, when available
robust liveness detection checks that can assist failover to the second VPN tunnel

evidence.quote: We recommend that you use BGP-capable devices, when available, because the BGP protocol offers robust liveness detection checks that can assist failover to the second VPN tunnel if the first tunnel goes down.

claim: With a device that does not support BGP advertising, you select static routing and enter the IP prefixes of your network. With a BGP device you do not specify static routes, because the device advertises its routes itself.
question: What do you enter for a Site-to-Site VPN connection with static routing, and what with BGP?

values.display: you must select static routing and enter the routes (IP prefixes) for your network
you don't specify static routes to the Site-to-Site VPN connection

evidence.quote: If you use a device that supports BGP advertising, you don't specify static routes to the Site-to-Site VPN connection because the device uses BGP to advertise its routes to the virtual private gateway. If you use a device that doesn't support BGP advertising, you must select static routing and enter the routes (IP prefixes) for your network that should be communicated to the virtual private gateway.

claim: The VPC route table uses the most specific route that matches the traffic (longest prefix match). A local route is preferred over overlapping propagated routes from a VPN or Direct Connect connection, even if the propagated routes are more specific.
question: Which route wins in a VPC route table when routes overlap, and how do propagated VPN routes compare with the local route?

values.display: the most specific route in your route table that matches the traffic
the local route is most preferred even if the propagated routes are more specific

qualifiers.scope: VPC route table with propagated routes

evidence.quote:
We use the most specific route in your route table that matches the traffic to determine how to route the traffic (longest prefix match). If your route table has overlapping or matching routes, the following rules apply:
If propagated routes from a Site-to-Site VPN connection or Direct Connect connection overlap with the local route for your VPC, the local route is most preferred even if the propagated routes are more specific.

claim: When the prefixes are the same, a virtual private gateway prefers BGP routes from a Direct Connect connection first, then manually added static routes of a Site-to-Site VPN connection, then BGP routes from a Site-to-Site VPN connection.
question: For the same prefix, which path does a virtual private gateway prefer: Direct Connect or Site-to-Site VPN?

values.display: BGP propagated routes from an Direct Connect connection
values.spoken: Direct Connect BGP routes come first

values.display: from most preferred to least preferred

qualifiers.scope: virtual private gateway route selection for identical prefixes

evidence.quote:
If the prefixes are the same, then the virtual private gateway prioritizes routes as follows, from most preferred to least preferred:
BGP propagated routes from an Direct Connect connection
Blackhole routes are not propagated to a Site-to-Site VPN customer gateway via BGP.
Manually added static routes for a Site-to-Site VPN connection
BGP propagated routes from a Site-to-Site VPN connection

claim: For matching prefixes where each Site-to-Site VPN connection uses BGP, the prefix with the shortest AS PATH is preferred.
question: How are BGP routes compared when several Site-to-Site VPN connections advertise the same prefix?

values.display: the prefix with the shortest AS PATH is preferred
the AS PATH is compared

qualifiers.scope: Site-to-Site VPN connections that use BGP

evidence.quote: For matching prefixes where each Site-to-Site VPN connection uses BGP, the AS PATH is compared and the prefix with the shortest AS PATH is preferred.

claim: The health of a tunnel endpoint takes precedence over other routing attributes, for VPNs on virtual private gateways and on transit gateways.
question: What takes precedence over other routing attributes when a VPN tunnel is selected?

values.display: The health of a tunnel endpoint takes precedence over other routing attributes
VPNs on virtual private gateways and Transit Gateways

qualifiers.scope: VPNs on virtual private gateways and transit gateways

evidence.quote: The health of a tunnel endpoint takes precedence over other routing attributes. This precedence applies to VPNs on virtual private gateways and Transit Gateways.

claim: When a propagated VPN or Direct Connect route has the same destination CIDR block as an existing static route, the static route is preferred (for example a route whose target is an internet gateway or virtual private gateway).
question: Which route is used when a propagated route and a static route have the same destination CIDR block?

values.display: we prioritize the static routes
have the same destination CIDR block as other existing static routes

evidence.quote: If propagated routes from a Site-to-Site VPN connection or Direct Connect connection have the same destination CIDR block as other existing static routes (longest prefix match cannot be applied), we prioritize the static routes whose targets are an internet gateway, a virtual private gateway, a network interface, an instance ID, a VPC peering connection, a NAT gateway, a transit gateway, or a gateway VPC endpoint.

claim: On a virtual private gateway, one tunnel across all VPN connections on the gateway is selected, and ECMP is not supported. ECMP is supported for Site-to-Site VPN connections on a transit gateway.
question: Can a virtual private gateway use several VPN tunnels at once with ECMP?

values.display: ECMP is not supported for Site-to-Site VPN connections on a virtual private gateway
ECMP, which is supported for Site-to-Site VPN connections on a transit gateway

qualifiers.scope: virtual private gateway versus transit gateway

evidence.quote: For a virtual private gateway, one tunnel across all Site-to-Site VPN connections on the gateway will be selected. To use more than one tunnel, we recommend exploring Equal Cost Multipath (ECMP), which is supported for Site-to-Site VPN connections on a transit gateway. For more information, see Transit gateways in Amazon VPC Transit Gateways. ECMP is not supported for Site-to-Site VPN connections on a virtual private gateway.

claim: On a transit gateway you can use ECMP to get higher VPN bandwidth by aggregating several VPN tunnels. The VPN connection must use dynamic routing; ECMP is not supported with static routing.
question: What routing type does ECMP across VPN tunnels require?

values.display: the VPN connection must be configured for dynamic routing
ECMP is not supported on VPN connections that use static routing

qualifiers.scope: Site-to-Site VPN connections on a transit gateway

evidence.quote: For Site-to-Site VPN connections on a transit gateway, you can use ECMP to get higher VPN bandwidth by aggregating multiple VPN tunnels. To use ECMP, the VPN connection must be configured for dynamic routing. ECMP is not supported on VPN connections that use static routing.

claim: In the VPC route table you add a route for the remote network with the virtual private gateway as target. You can also enable route propagation so that network routes are added to the table automatically.
question: How do VPN routes get into the VPC route table when you use a virtual private gateway?

values.display: you must add a route for your remote network and specify the virtual private gateway as the target
enable route propagation for your route table

qualifiers.scope: VPC route table of a VPC with a virtual private gateway

evidence.quote: In your VPC route table, you must add a route for your remote network and specify the virtual private gateway as the target. This enables traffic from your VPC that's destined for your remote network to route via the virtual private gateway and over one of the VPN tunnels. You can enable route propagation for your route table to automatically propagate your network routes to the table for you.

claim: Accelerated Site-to-Site VPN makes the user experience more consistent by using the highly available and congestion-free AWS global network instead of multiple public internet networks.
question: Why use an accelerated Site-to-Site VPN?

values.display: makes user experience more consistent
the highly available and congestion-free AWS global network

evidence.quote: VPN connections face inconsistent availability and performance as traffic traverses through multiple public networks on the internet before reaching the VPN endpoint in AWS. These public networks can be congested. Each hop can introduce availability and performance risks. Accelerated Site-to-Site VPN makes user experience more consistent by using the highly available and congestion-free AWS global network.

claim: AWS VPN CloudHub lets several Site-to-Site VPN connections give your sites secure communication with each other, not only with the VPC. It uses a hub-and-spoke model that works with or without a VPC and is suited to branch offices that already have internet connections.

Both devices should advertise the same IP ranges to the virtual private gateway. We use BGP routing to determine the path for traffic. If one customer gateway device fails, the virtual private gateway directs all traffic to the working customer gateway device.
